================================================================================
1. SYSTEM OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE
================================================================================
OpenSMS converts any Android smartphone or tablet (running Android 7.0 / API 24 to Android 15+ / API 36) into a high-performance, private, 24/7 SMS Gateway.

Key Components:
- Background Gateway Server: FastAPI application powered by Uvicorn running inside a Python service on Android.
- SQLite WAL Persistence: High-throughput local relational store operating in Write-Ahead Logging mode (`PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`) with busy timeouts. Keeps message history, delivery statuses (`queued`, `submitted`, `sent`, `delivered`, `failed`, `unknown`), multi-key token registry, and telemetry metrics.
- Telephony Orchestration Engine: Built via PyJNIus interacting directly with native Android `SmsManager` and `SubscriptionManager`. Handles GSM-7 vs UCS-2 character classification, multipart segmentation, and dual-SIM routing.
- Tailscale awareness: OpenSMS observes the phone's Tailscale address (a VPN network carrying `100.64.0.0/10` or `fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48`) from the official Tailscale app and shows status and diagnostics. It does not join the tailnet itself and stores no Tailscale credential. An API listening mode (all networks / Tailscale only / this phone) can restrict who can connect.
- Auto-Updater Subsystem: Queries the configured repository's GitHub Releases, accepts only release-asset URLs of that repository, verifies the published SHA-256 when available, then tries to open the Android Package Installer (falling back to opening the release page in the browser).

Default Configuration:
- Port: 9292 (configurable from 1025 to 65535)
- Binding: 0.0.0.0 (listens on Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and Tailscale VPN interfaces)

================================================================================
2. WHAT'S NEW IN VERSION 0.4.0
================================================================================
- In-App GitHub Releases Auto-Updater: Detects newer releases on app launch, displays an animated notification banner on Home screen, and supports 1-tap in-app APK download and install.
- SQLite Message Store & Metrics: Replaced ephemeral in-memory state with SQLite WAL persistence. Tracks delivery receipts, carrier errors, sent today count, success rate %, and queue depth.
- Dual-SIM Telephony Routing: Multi-SIM autodetection via Android `SubscriptionManager`. Allows carrier slot selection in Settings (Auto, SIM 1, SIM 2) and programmatic routing via `sim_slot` in the REST API.
- Multi-Token API Security: Allows multiple named API keys with enforced scopes (`sms:write`, `sms:read`, `admin`) and individual revocation (`DELETE /keys/{id}` with an `admin` key, or the API tab in the app).
- Expanded REST API: Added `GET /sms/{id}`, `GET /sms/history/`, `GET /system/stats/`, `GET /system/sims/`, and `GET /system/update/`.
- UI/UX & Bug Fixes: Guarded settings switches against KivyMD 2.x event loops (BUG-03 fix) and added background-to-foreground IPC activity heartbeats.

================================================================================
3. NETWORK TOPOLOGY & CROSS-NETWORK CONNECTIVITY
================================================================================
OpenSMS binds to all network interfaces on the device:
1. Local Wi-Fi / LAN: Accessible at `http://192.168.x.x:9292` by other machines on the same local router.
2. Tailscale (Recommended): With the Tailscale app connected on the phone, accessible at `http://100.x.y.z:9292` from any device in the same tailnet, without port forwarding.
3. Reverse SSH Tunnel: Using Termux on Android: `ssh -N -R 9292:localhost:9292 user@vps.com`.
4. Cloudflare Tunnel / Ngrok: Accessible via public HTTPS URL if exposed through a tunnel agent.

================================================================================
4. AUTHENTICATION & SECURITY MODEL
================================================================================
- Mechanism: Bearer Token authentication via HTTP Header:
    Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
- Token format: High-entropy string generated with `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` prefixed with `osms_`.
- Storage: Tokens are hashed with SHA-256 before insertion into SQLite. Plaintext tokens are wiped from RAM after generation.
- Rate Limiting: 10 failed authentication attempts per client address within a 60-second window trigger an HTTP 429 response; each key may send at most 300 messages per minute.

================================================================================
5. COMPLETE REST API SPECIFICATIONS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5.1. Liveness Health Check
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GET /health/
No authentication required.

Response (200 OK):
{
  "status": "ok",
  "service": "OpenSMS",
  "version": "0.4.0"
}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5.2. Send Single SMS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
POST /sms/
Authentication: Bearer <API_KEY>

Request Body:
{
  "number": "+1234567890",       // Required: E.164 phone number
  "text": "Hello from OpenSMS!", // Required: SMS content
  "sim_slot": 0                  // Optional: 0 for SIM 1, 1 for SIM 2 (default: system preference)
}

Response (200 OK):
{
  "id": "3f2b8c1a-9d4e-4a6b-8c2d-7e1f0a5b9c42",
  "number": "+1234567890",
  "stat": true,
  "sim_slot": 0,
  "segments": 1,
  "encoding": "GSM-7"
}

Errors:
- 400 Bad Request: Number format invalid or text empty.
- 401 Unauthorized: Invalid or missing API key.
- 429 Too Many Requests: Rate limit exceeded.
- 502 Bad Gateway (`delivery_failed`): the hand-off to the telephony layer failed (see `detail`).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5.3. Send Batch SMS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
POST /sms/batch/
Authentication: Bearer <API_KEY>

Request Body (up to 100 messages):
{
  "sim_slot": 0,
  "messages": [
    { "number": "+1234567890", "text": "Notification 1" },
    { "number": "+1987654321", "text": "Notification 2" }
  ]
}

Response (200 OK):
{
  "batch_id": "batch_98fbc102",
  "total": 2,
  "successful": 2,
  "failed": 0,
  "results": [
    { "id": "msg_01", "number": "+1234567890", "stat": true },
    { "id": "msg_02", "number": "+1987654321", "stat": true }
  ]
}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5.4. Get SMS Status by ID
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GET /sms/{id}
Authentication: Bearer <API_KEY>

Response (200 OK):
{
  "id": "3f2b8c1a-9d4e-4a6b-8c2d-7e1f0a5b9c42",
  "recipient": "+1234567890",
  "text": "Hello from OpenSMS!",
  "encoding": "GSM-7",
  "segments": 1,
  "sim_slot": 0,
  "status": "sent", // "queued" | "submitted" | "sent" | "delivered" | "failed" | "unknown"
  "created_at": 1729432800.12,
  "delivered_at": null,
  "carrier_error": null
}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5.5. List SMS History
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GET /sms/history/?limit=50&offset=0&status=all&search=+1234
Authentication: Bearer <API_KEY>

Response (200 OK):
{
  "count": 1,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 50,
  "messages": [
    {
      "id": "3f2b8c1a-9d4e-4a6b-8c2d-7e1f0a5b9c42",
      "recipient": "+1234567890",
      "text": "Hello from OpenSMS!",
      "status": "sent",
      "encoding": "GSM-7",
      "segments": 1,
      "sim_slot": 0,
      "created_at": 1729432800.12,
      "delivered_at": null
    }
  ]
}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5.6. Get System Stats & Telemetry
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GET /system/stats/
Authentication: Bearer <API_KEY>

Response (200 OK):
{
  "app": "OpenSMS",
  "version": "0.4.0",
  "metrics": {
    "sent_today": 142,
    "failed_today": 1,
    "success_rate": 99.3,
    "queue_depth": 0
  }
}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5.7. Get Active SIM Slots
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GET /system/sims/
Authentication: Bearer <API_KEY>

Response (200 OK):
{
  "count": 2,
  "sims": [
    { "slot": 0, "carrier": "T-Mobile", "country": "us", "active": true },
    { "slot": 1, "carrier": "AT&T", "country": "us", "active": true }
  ]
}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5.8. Check for App Updates
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GET /system/update/
Authentication: Bearer <API_KEY>

Response (200 OK):
{
  "success": true,
  "has_update": false,
  "current_version": "0.4.0",
  "latest_version": "0.4.0",
  "tag_name": "v0.4.0",
  "release_name": "OpenSMS v0.4.0",
  "release_notes": "Added SQLite WAL persistence and auto-updater.",
  "html_url": "https://github.com/ShanudhaTirosh/OpenSMS/releases/tag/v0.4.0",
  "apk_url": "https://github.com/.../OpenSMS.apk",
  "apk_size": 18452100
}

================================================================================
6. DUAL-SIM TELEPHONY & SMS SEGMENTATION RULES
================================================================================
Character Encoding & Segment Calculation:
- Standard GSM 7-bit alphabet:
  - Single SMS: up to 160 characters.
  - Multi-part SMS: 153 characters per segment (7 bytes reserved for UDH header).
- Unicode (UCS-2) encoding (triggered when emojis, Cyrillic, Arabic, Chinese, etc. are used):
  - Single SMS: up to 70 characters.
  - Multi-part SMS: 67 characters per segment.

Dual-SIM Selection:
- If `sim_slot` is omitted in the API request, the gateway uses the user's preferred SIM slot configured in the app settings, or the Android OS default subscription.
- Set `sim_slot: 0` for SIM 1, or `sim_slot: 1` for SIM 2.

================================================================================
7. MULTI-LANGUAGE CODE INTEGRATION RECIPES
================================================================================

--- 7.1. Python (requests) ---
```python
import requests

url = "http://100.85.x.x:9292/sms/"
headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer osms_your_secret_key",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
payload = {
    "number": "+1234567890",
    "text": "Hello from Python!",
    "sim_slot": 0
}
res = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(res.json())
```

--- 7.2. Python (httpx async) ---
```python
import asyncio
import httpx

async def send_sms():
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        res = await client.post(
            "http://100.85.x.x:9292/sms/",
            json={"number": "+1234567890", "text": "Async SMS dispatched!"},
            headers={"Authorization": "Bearer osms_your_secret_key"}
        )
        return res.json()

asyncio.run(send_sms())
```

--- 7.3. Node.js & TypeScript (fetch) ---
```typescript
interface SmsResponse {
  id: string;
  number: string;
  stat: boolean;
  sim_slot: number;
}

async function sendSms(number: string, text: string): Promise<SmsResponse> {
  const res = await fetch("http://100.85.x.x:9292/sms/", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "Authorization": "Bearer osms_your_secret_key",
      "Content-Type": "application/json"
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ number, text, sim_slot: 0 })
  });

  if (!res.ok) {
    throw new Error(`SMS send failed with status ${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`);
  }
  return res.json() as Promise<SmsResponse>;
}
```

--- 7.4. Go ---
```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
)

func main() {
	payload, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]interface{}{
		"number":   "+1234567890",
		"text":     "Alert from Go service",
		"sim_slot": 0,
	})

	req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "http://100.85.x.x:9292/sms/", bytes.NewBuffer(payload))
	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer osms_your_secret_key")
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")

	client := &http.Client{}
	resp, err := client.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	fmt.Println("Status:", resp.Status)
}
```

--- 7.5. cURL ---
```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://100.85.x.x:9292/sms/' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer osms_your_secret_key' \
  -d '{"number": "+1234567890", "text": "Verification Code: 948192"}'
```

--- 7.6. PHP ---
```php
<?php
$ch = curl_init('http://100.85.x.x:9292/sms/');
$payload = json_encode([
    'number' => '+1234567890',
    'text' => 'Hello from PHP Backend',
    'sim_slot' => 0
]);

curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, $payload);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, [
    'Content-Type: application/json',
    'Authorization: Bearer osms_your_secret_key'
]);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, true);
$result = curl_exec($ch);
curl_close($ch);
echo $result;
?>
```

--- 7.7. Rust (reqwest) ---
```rust
use reqwest::header::{HeaderMap, HeaderValue, AUTHORIZATION, CONTENT_TYPE};
use serde_json::json;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
    headers.insert(AUTHORIZATION, HeaderValue::from_static("Bearer osms_your_secret_key"));
    headers.insert(CONTENT_TYPE, HeaderValue::from_static("application/json"));

    let client = reqwest::Client::new();
    let body = json!({
        "number": "+1234567890",
        "text": "Dispatched via Rust!"
    });

    let resp = client.post("http://100.85.x.x:9292/sms/")
        .headers(headers)
        .json(&body)
        .send()
        .await?;

    println!("Response: {:?}", resp.text().await?);
    Ok(())
}
```

8. AI AGENT TOOL-CALLING SCHEMAS
================================================================================

OpenAI Function Schema:
```json
{
  "type": "function",
  "function": {
    "name": "send_sms",
    "description": "Send a real cellular SMS text message to a recipient phone number via the OpenSMS Android gateway.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "number": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "Recipient phone number with country code in E.164 format (e.g. +1234567890)."
        },
        "text": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "The message body text to send."
        },
        "sim_slot": {
          "type": "integer",
          "description": "Optional: 0 for SIM 1, 1 for SIM 2."
        }
      },
      "required": ["number", "text"]
    }
  }
}
```

Anthropic Claude Tool Schema:
```json
{
  "name": "send_sms",
  "description": "Send a real cellular SMS text message via the OpenSMS Android gateway.",
  "input_schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "number": { "type": "string", "description": "Destination phone number in E.164 format" },
      "text": { "type": "string", "description": "SMS text content" },
      "sim_slot": { "type": "integer", "description": "Optional: 0 for SIM 1, 1 for SIM 2" }
    },
    "required": ["number", "text"]
  }
}
```

Model Context Protocol (MCP) Tool Declaration:
```json
{
  "name": "send_sms",
  "description": "Dispatches a real SMS message via connected OpenSMS Android phone.",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "number": { "type": "string", "description": "Recipient phone number in E.164 format" },
      "text": { "type": "string", "description": "SMS text message content" },
      "sim_slot": { "type": "integer", "description": "SIM slot: 0 or 1" }
    },
    "required": ["number", "text"]
  }
}
```

================================================================================
9. ERROR CODES & TROUBLESHOOTING
================================================================================
- 400 Bad Request: Number must contain between 7 and 15 digits. Text cannot be empty or only whitespace.
- 401 Unauthorized: The Bearer token provided does not match any registered key or has been revoked.
- 429 Too Many Requests: More than 10 failed authentication requests from the caller's address in the last 60 seconds, or the per-key send limit was exceeded (see `Retry-After`).
- 502 Bad Gateway: The hand-off to the telephony layer failed. Check cellular reception, carrier balance/allowance and SIM status.
- 503 Service Unavailable: The send queue is full; retry after `Retry-After`.
- Battery Sleeping / Disconnect: Ensure OpenSMS battery optimization is set to "Unrestricted" in Android settings.
- Android 13+ SMS Permission: Enable "Allow restricted settings" in Android App Info if permissions are greyed out.
